transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Silver Peak CTO), Melissa Chen (Head of Cloud Ops), Ravi Patel (Security Architect)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Silver Peak Bank's regulatory constraints - GDPR cross-border, financial services logging retention, and potential HIPAA scope for a small health-benefit product. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment and asking about KMS/HSM, audit logs limits, and data residency guarantees.

Topics covered: GDPR residency controls, Private/VPC options, Dedicated capacity SLA and benchmarking, logging/Audit retention and redaction, encryption and key management, compliance doc requests.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We wanted to do a quick discovery on data residency and compliance requirements for the Silver Peak project. Priya and I from Redwood, and I think Tom, Melissa, Ravi from your side, is that right?
[00:08] Tom: Yep that's right, Tom here. Quick heads up, we're on a tight timeline, pilot in Q2, decision by end of month if possible.
[00:14] Melissa: Melissa here. We're mainly worried about where data lives and what logs contain - legal has a long list.
[00:20] Ravi: Ravi - security architect. We also need to understand key management, auditability, and whether any HIPs or PII can leave the EU for GDPR.
[00:28] Priya: Great - quick intro from our side: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Hosted is fastest but data may transit regions; Dedicated gives reserved capacity in region, and Private offers VPC/on-prem for strict residency. We'll walk through tradeoffs.
[00:39] Tom: Can you define "Hosted may transit regions" - are you saying tokens or payloads might go to the US? We can't permit EU customer PII to leave the region.
[00:48] Jordan: Right - our Hosted control plane is global and in some cases the inference happens in region, but metadata and logs can be centralized depending on plan. For strict EU-only residency we recommend Dedicated pinned to an EU region, or Private with VPC or on-prem install.
[00:58] Melissa: What's included in logs? Our legal team wants minimal logging of prompts and responses; we need audit traces but not full prompt storage. Is redaction available?
[01:08] Priya: We have configurable logging. By default we capture request/response metadata, latencies, error traces, and optional request body. For privacy-sensitive workloads we can disable storing full prompt text, only store hashes and audit metadata. There are some SLMs and retention settings you can configure.
[01:23] Ravi: Sorry, SLMs?
[01:24] Priya: Sorry, I meant SLAs and storage retention - bad abbreviation.
[01:27] Tom: Right. On encryption - do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS? We need to control the keys for production.
[01:34] Jordan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS keys, including HSM integrations via our KMS provider partners. Hosted can use our managed keys but we also offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on enterprise plans.
[01:46] Melissa: What about audit logs retention? Regulators require 7 years for some records. Can you store immutable audit logs that long and export them to our S3 retention bucket?
[01:55] Priya: We can keep audit logs for configurable retention; for Dedicated/Private we can ship logs to your S3 or to your SIEM. Immutable retention for 7+ years is supported via external archival - we'd recommend exporting to your archive bucket.
[02:07] Ravi: Are those logs readable? We want to avoid storing PII in logs. Is redaction automatic?
[02:12] Jordan: We offer automatic redaction patterns and PII scrubbing on ingest; you can also opt to not record request/response bodies and only record the hashed fingerprints for traceability. That will meet many regulator needs.
[02:22] Tom: On GDPR, is there a Data Processing Addendum and Data Transfer Agreement? Will you sign SCCs?
[02:28] Priya: Yes - DPA and SCCs are part of our enterprise contract. For Private deployments, data doesn't leave customer control, but we still provide contractual guarantees. We'll send the DPA and standard SCC language.
[02:37] Melissa: HIPAA - we have a small line of business that touches health benefits. Do you have a BA agreement and HIPAA controls?
[02:43] Jordan: We support HIPAA for customers who contract for coverage. We can sign a BAA for Dedicated/Private; Hosted can be covered under enterprise agreements with additional logging controls. Priya can follow up with required safeguards.
[02:54] Priya: For HIPAA, we'd recommend Dedicated or Private so logs and PHI never leave your VPC and keys are customer-managed.
[03:02] Ravi: Network-wise, how does VPC peering work? Can we keep inference nodes inside our subnet and restrict egress?
[03:09] Priya: For Private we deploy a control plane with optional data plane in your VPC - nodes can be inside your subnet and egress rules are fully under your control. For Dedicated we can provision instances in an isolated account/region with VPC peering and strict firewall rules.
[03:21] Tom: Performance concerns - our latency SLO is 200ms p95 for simple prompts. Dedicated gives predictable latency but at what cost? Also, do you do KV cache? I saw references to KV cash in some docs which confused legal.
[03:33] Jordan: (laughs) KV cache - yes it's KV cache, sorry for typos in docs. Dedicated helps meet predictable p95 because of reserved GPU pools and less noisy neighbors. Cost varies by model and quantization; we'll send you cost estimates. We also do prefix and KV caching to speed repeat requests.
[03:47] Melissa: If we do Private on-prem, do you support our custom hardware or do we need to use your image?
[03:53] Priya: We have an on-prem package that supports common NVIDIA stacks; custom hardware may require additional ops work. We recommend a short vetting phase during onboarding.
[04:02] Ravi: About audits - what about field-level logging? We need certain fields captured for RMF and internal audits - user_id, request_id, model_version, timestamp, route. Can you guarantee those are always present and tamper-evident?
[04:14] Jordan: Yes - audit schema is configurable and we can make those fields mandatory. For tamper-evidence, we support log signing and export to an immutable store (e.g., WORM S3) or SIEM with append-only retention.
[04:26] Tom: Any gotchas with data residency and model fallback? For example, if regional capacity is saturated, will you fall back to a US-hosted model? That's a dealbreaker.
[04:34] Priya: Good question. We have routing policies: by default we route to region-specific capacity. For Hosted accounts it's possible to route to fallback pools unless you pin to Dedicated/Private. For your case, we'd recommend pinning to EU Dedicated or using Private so fallback to other regions is disabled.
[04:47] Ravi: Does pinning mean we'd lose automatic updates or model improvements?
[04:50] Jordan: Not at all - pinning is about where inference runs, not model updates. You can pin region and still get model version updates; rollouts are controlled by your policy.
[04:58] Melissa: For encryption-in-transit and at-rest, do you use customer TLS and certificates or Redwood-managed?
[05:04] Priya: We support both. For Dedicated/Private you can provide certs and we can terminate inside your VPC. Hosted uses Redwood-managed certs, but you can request mutual TLS.
[05:13] Tom: Ok - procurement will want pricing for Dedicated and Private, plus assumed throughput for the pilot. Also want SOC2 and penetration test reports.
[05:20] Jordan: We'll include SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and recent pentest report in the package. We'll also include a pricing sheet with throughput tiers and a recommended benchmark plan.
[05:29] Ravi: About logs exclusions - can we exclude certain routes from logging or obfuscate tokens fully? We have a payments route that must not store card PANs.
[05:36] Priya: Yes, route-level logging rules are supported. You can configure route policies to strip or redact sensitive fields before storage. We'll add examples in the docs we send.
[05:44] Melissa: Who at Redwood will be our contact during the pilot?
[05:47] Jordan: I'll be your AE, Priya is the SE for technical questions, and you'll get an onboarding CSM if you go to pilot. We'll also loop in the infra team for the deep-dive.
[05:56] Tom: Sounds good. Timeline: we'll review legal and make a go/no-go internally by 2026-03-12. If we get the docs and pricing this week we'll be able to lock dates.
[06:05] Jordan: Perfect. Quick recap and next steps then.

Recap and Next Steps (from call):
- Jordan to email SOC2/ISO docs, BAA template, and SCC/DPA paperwork.
- Priya to draft benchmarking plan and config suggestions (batching, quantization) and recommend Dedicated capacity for the pilot.
- Provide pricing sheet for Dedicated vs Private, include estimated p95 costs and throughput tiers.
- Ravi to send required audit fields and retention policy so we can validate schema.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with infra team w/c 2026-03-11.

Action items (explicit):
[06:20] Jordan: I'll send the contract docs and SOC2 by tomorrow EOD.
